supportingConnections.hypothesis: Seeing the graph as a graph shows structure, clusters and orphans that no list reveals, so humans and agents agree on the same picture.
The keyboard-driven list is where daily work happens: fast navigation and editing decide whether people keep their plans in Aimparency at all.
A watchdog the human can read and steer from the UI makes autonomous agent runs visible, so cooperation does not become blind delegation.
Views are only as good as what carries them: fast, live, consistent loading and feedback make every view trustworthy.
The human stays the final authority only if checking agent work in the UI is quick.
supportingConnections.reflection: Unclear so far. The review queue did shrink (197 to 1 on 2026-11-01, commit 708a52af), but through a policy change (verified work goes straight to implemented), not because the inbox made checking quicker. The inbox's own effect on review latency was never measured.

status.comment: Container: it never finishes, it keeps collecting UI work (Felix 2026-10-17: containers can always be filled with ideas). Its children carry the review state.
